(2026) PLOS ONE 21(7):e0352176 ('we used (5) the Self-transcendence Inventory [33] composed of 10 items'). The S1 Table's other blocks (PoT judgments, BDI, STAI, FFMQ, happiness questionnaires) are separate columns and separate IRW tables; only the STI block is here. WORDS: the paper's Table 6 (10.1371/journal.pone.0352176.t006) prints all 10 items in full, numbered 1-10, as row labels of the item-level correlation matrix. That table is an IMAGE -- grep over the scraped article text returns nothing -- so it was read from the PNG at journals.plos.org/plosone/article/figure/image?size=large&id=10.1371/journal.pone.0352176.t006 and transcribed by eye; a human spot-check of punctuation is worth one minute. Transcribed literally: item 8 ends WITHOUT a full stop in the source and ships that way, and item 3's published English is 'I do not become angry as easily' (the ASTI's own 25-item present-tense form reads 'I do not become angry easily') -- nothing was normalised toward canonical ASTI wording. LANGUAGE: the study is French (Clermont-Ferrand, French ethics committee) and the S1 Table's STI column headers are French. No full French wording is published anywhere in the deposit or the paper -- the headers carry only truncated CamelCase fragments (STI2_esChosesMaterielles, STI5_eRessensBeaucoupPlus are cut on the LEFT; STI7_IlEstPlusFacilede and STI9_JeSensDavantage stop mid-sentence), and S1 Table is the article's only Supporting Information file. So the paper's English ships in the base fields with language=French and no _translated columns -- the documented fallback, same call as the sibling monier_2026_pot in batch_109. ANCHORS: the paper states the 7-point anchors for its PoT questions and its happiness questionnaires but says nothing at all about the STI response scale (the live data run 1-7; the ASTI's canonical form is 1-4, so canonical anchors would have been wrong as well as unsourced). option_text therefore ships blank for all of resp 1-7 rather than padded with the numbers themselves, and instructions/section_prompt are NA for the same reason -- no administered instruction text is recoverable. MAPPING: recorded paper_explicit rather than data_labels because the shipped WORDS come from the paper's numbering, not from the headers (the headers hold fragments, not items). It is nevertheless verified end to end, not inferred: all 70 cells of Table 6 recompute from the S1 Table columns to within 0.0054 (printed to 2 dp), each S1 column's nearest published row is its own with a 14x-48x margin over the best wrong row, and per-item n from irw_table_sets() matches the raw column counts 10/10 (101/105/105/104/104/104/103/104/104/105). See verify_monier_2026_sti.R. The French header fragments independently agree with all 10 English items (STI6_JeTrouvePlusdeJoieDansLaVie / 'I find more joy in life'; STI10_JeMinquieteMoins / 'I have become less concerned about other people's opinions of me'). RIGHTS: no restriction locatable for the ASTI and so nothing to quote -- there is no ASTI/Levenson row in instrument_rights_register.csv, no publisher sells it (it was published in a journal article, Int J Aging Hum Dev 2005;60(2):127-43), its items are reproduced openly in the CRAN package MPsychoR's ASTI help page and in this CC BY 4.0 PLOS article, and searches surfaced no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause from Levenson or any rights holder. Silence is permission, so the rights rule does not fire. A register row for the ASTI would be a reasonable add for a later pass.

Pass with caveat. `motion` is O'Brien & Yeatman 2021 (Dev Sci 24:e13039) random-dot motion discrimination in 106 children; source data github.com/yeatmanlab/Parametric_public Analysis/Clean_Motion_Data.csv (CC BY 4.0 per the IRW biblio row). It is a psychophysical task, not a questionnaire, so there is no transcribable item wording: the item code is paste(block, stim) and each 'item' is a stimulus condition (block 1-6 x motion coherence 6/12/24/48/100%). item_text is therefore a CONSTRUCTED stimulus description ('Random-dot motion stimulus at 6% coherence (block 1 of 6)'), not a transcript. The words that ARE verbatim are the instructions, read off the study's own on-screen images in Motion/Exp/ of the same repo: Instruction2.jpg ('Which way are the stars going?', the practice screen) and Instructions.jpg ('Left motion = left arrow / Right motion = right arrow / Hit SPACE to continue / Hit ESC to exit', shown before each block by RunMotionDisc.m). The four on-screen line breaks are rendered as ' / '. resp is scored accuracy, not the direction the child pressed (RunMotionDisc.m: result.response = keyResponse == config.dir/180), so option_text carries Incorrect/Correct and correct_response is 1; the correct direction itself varies trial to trial and is not recoverable at the item level. No rights restriction: the task is lab-built and its code and stimuli are published in the authors' own open repository; no clause reserving a right was found for the instrument. Retry test: NO -- this is not a block, the table shipped.

Pass with caveat. Item stems and response categories come from the MPsychoR package's own AvalanchePrep.Rd documentation (Format section labels each of the four columns info/discuss/gear/decision; Description lists that column's response categories in order). The Haegeli, Gunn & Haider (2012) Prevention Science source paper (doi 10.1007/s11121-012-0282-5) is paywalled -- link.springer.com 303s to an IdP login -- so the administered survey wording could not be checked against the .Rd's rendering; the .Rd labels are terse summaries ('Check avalanche danger information.') and are shipped as-is rather than expanded. Caveat: the .Rd never prints '1 = ...', so the resp<->option_text mapping is inferred from the Description's listing order; verified as far as direction (all four items intercorrelate +0.10 to +0.45 under that reading, so no item is listed backwards) but not for the internal order of middle categories. Option text is transcribed verbatim from running prose, so it retains the .Rd's sentence-flow lowercasing and its odd 'do not check or Do not know' capitalisation. No rights restriction: four ad-hoc survey questions distributed on CRAN, no named commercial instrument, nothing in instrument_rights_register.csv.
